orders.description: Plaintiff’s limited appeal from the August 16, 2017 dismissal order.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted defendants’ motion for summary judgment dismissing the amended complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on snow and ice on an exterior stairway landing at defendants’ premises on February 28, 2015. He advanced a defective-awning explanation for the accumulation.

legal_issues.finding: Defendants established that they lacked a reasonable opportunity to remedy the storm-created accumulation before the fall; plaintiff raised no triable issue.
Plaintiff’s defective-awning explanation for the snow/ice was speculative in light of his weather testimony and did not raise a triable issue.

evidence_discussed.description: Plaintiff’s deposition regarding weather conditions undermined his defective-awning theory; the opinion does not quote those weather details.

quality.notes: Private ownership and slip mechanism are explicit. Premises use and injured role are unknown. The court establishes no reasonable remediation opportunity under the storm rule, not an express finding that precipitation was falling at the exact accident time. No weather records or expert are specifically identified. The awning explanation remains an allegation rejected as speculative; no awning defect, actual/constructive notice or negligent creation finding is inferred. Whole appealed dismissal is affirmed.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed insofar as appealed from, with costs.
On February 28, 2015, the plaintiff allegedly was injured when he slipped and fell on snow and ice on a landing of an exterior stairway at premises owned by the defendants.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Westchester County (Charles D. Wood, J.), dated August 16, 2017. The order, insofar as appealed from, granted the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the amended complaint.

Here, the defendants established their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law by demonstrating that they did not have a reasonable opportunity to remedy the snow and ice condition that was created by the storm prior to the plaintiff's fall
The plaintiff, in opposition, failed to raise a triable issue of fact

Given the plaintiff's deposition testimony regarding the weather conditions, his claim that the snow and ice condition was caused by a defective awning was speculative and, therefore, insufficient to raise a triable issue of fact
Accordingly, we agree with the Supreme Court's determination to grant the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the amended complaint.
The Supreme Court, inter alia, granted the defendants' motion, and the plaintiff appeals. We affirm.

orders.description: Defendants’ appeal and plaintiff’s cross-appeal from the single April 27, 2020 order.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied dismissal of common-law negligence claims, granted dismissal of Dram Shop claims, and directed a negative-inference charge for lost surveillance.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on liquid from a spilled drink while dancing at a wedding reception at defendants’ premises in November 2016.

legal_issues.finding: Defendants’ own evidence demonstrated notice of the spill, but failed to establish adequate remediation or insufficient time to remedy it; negligence remained for trial.
Defendants were on notice of possible litigation and negligently failed to preserve accident video despite the preservation obligation; a negative-inference charge was upheld.
Defendants established no service of alcohol to a visibly intoxicated individual alleged to have spilled the drink; plaintiff raised no triable issue, so Dram Shop claims were dismissed.

evidence_discussed.description: Accident surveillance footage was unavailable because defendants negligently failed to preserve it; the court upheld a negative-inference sanction, not an inference based on footage independently viewed here.

Employees’ immediate accident documentation/investigation and plaintiff’s prompt insurance-information request supported notice of possible litigation and the preservation obligation; document formats are not specified.

Favors both reflects preserved negligence/sanction relief for plaintiff and preserved Dram Shop dismissal for defendants. The third-party caption does not make this a third-party-only appeal. evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed insofar as appealed and cross-appealed from, without costs or disbursements.

In November 2016, the plaintiff allegedly was injured when she slipped and fell on liquid on the floor of the defendants' premises while dancing at a wedding reception. The liquid substance allegedly was from a spilled drink.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the defendants appeal, and the plaintiff cross-appeals, from an order of the Supreme Court, Westchester County (Joan B. Lefkowitz, J.), dated April 27, 2020.

By order dated April 27, 2020, the Supreme Court denied that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the causes of action alleging common-law negligence, granted that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the causes of action alleging a violation of the Dram Shop Act, and granted the plaintiff's cross-motion to the extent of directing that a negative inference charge be given at trial against the defendants with respect to the unavailable video surveillance footage.

Here, the defendants established their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law dismissing the causes of action alleging a violation of the Dram Shop Act by demonstrating that they did not serve alcohol to any visibly intoxicated individual who allegedly spilled a drink on which the plaintiff slipped and fell
In opposition, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact. Therefore, the Supreme Court properly granted that branch of the defendants' motion.

Here, the evidence submitted by the defendants demonstrated that they had notice of the spill which allegedly caused the plaintiff's fall, and the defendants failed to establish, prima facie, that they adequately remedied that allegedly dangerous condition, or that they did not have a reasonable time to do so before the accident occurred
Since the defendants failed to meet their prima facie burden, the court properly denied that branch of their motion, regardless of the sufficiency of the opposition papers

Here, the plaintiff demonstrated that the defendants had an obligation to preserve video surveillance footage of the plaintiff's accident at the time of its destruction, but negligently failed to do so.

Considering the nature of the plaintiff's injuries, the immediate documentation and investigation into the cause of the accident by the defendants' employees, as well as the plaintiff's request within a couple of days of the accident for the defendants' insurance information, the defendants were clearly on notice of possible litigation and, thus, under an obligation to preserve any evidence that might be needed for future litigation

Under the circumstances of this case, the Supreme Court providently exercised its [*3] discretion in imposing a sanction of a negative inference charge against the defendants at trial with respect to the unavailable video surveillance footage

orders.description: Defendant’s appeal from the January 9, 2009 order denying summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendant’s motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff was leaving defendant’s supermarket on a temporary asphalt walkway during renovations when his foot slipped off its edge while making room for another patron. He fell through a flexible mesh fence into an excavation ditch; the timing of any slip on loose stones relative to his foot leaving the walkway remained unclear.

legal_issues.finding: Questions remained whether defendant provided reasonably safe ingress/egress at the temporary walkway and excavation edge, including an adequate barrier.
Even assuming defendant met its initial burden, the record left a factual issue whether it created the alleged unsafe walkway/barrier condition.
The court expressly found a factual issue as to actual notice of the alleged dangerous condition; no conclusive knowledge finding was made.
Specific checks for debris did not eliminate factual issues about constructive notice of the alleged unsafe barrier/walkway arrangement.

A jury could find the inadequate barrier a substantial cause despite the debris-focused defense. Deposition testimony was unclear about whether loose stones preceded or followed the foot leaving the walkway.
Factual issues would remain even if plaintiff’s expert affidavit were insufficient; the court did not decide that the affidavit was inadequate.

evidence_discussed.description: Plaintiff’s deposition did not clearly place any loose-stone slip before or after his foot slid off the walkway.
Store employees described checks minutes before and just after the accident, finding no stones or debris at the fall area.
Plaintiff submitted an opposing expert affidavit; defendant challenged sufficiency, but the court found other factual issues independently dispositive.

quality.notes: Express supermarket ownership and the temporary patron entrance/exit walkway support private premises. This is a customer’s personal slip followed by a fall into excavation, not an inferred construction-worker or Labor Law accident. Other hazard denotes inadequate barrier, hole the excavation ditch, and debris the disputed loose-stone account; no stones are treated as established cause. The court assumes rather than decides the initial burden and expert insufficiency, then identifies factual issues. Inspection evidence is testimony, not invented records. Accident date is unstated. No comparative-fault or code-violation holding is inferred.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed, with costs.

Plaintiff commenced this action seeking damages for injuries he sustained when he slipped and fell while exiting a supermarket owned by defendant located in the City of Johnstown, Fulton County. On the date of the accident, the supermarket was undergoing renovations, and a temporary asphalt walkway was being used for all patrons to enter and exit it. The temporary asphalt walkway was sectioned off from excavation work with a flexible orange mesh fence.

As plaintiff pushed his shopping cart out from the supermarket and onto the temporary asphalt walkway, he moved to the very left, alongside the flexible orange mesh fence, to make way for another patron to enter the supermarket. As he did so, plaintiffs foot slipped off the edge of the *1261 temporary asphalt walkway, causing him to fall through the flexible orange mesh fence into an excavation ditch and onto rebar, which was laid across the excavated ground.
Appeal from an order of the Supreme Court (Giardino, J.), entered January 9, 2009 in Fulton County, which denied defendant’s motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

To establish the lack of constructive notice, defendant offered the testimony from store employees that the temporary walkway was checked both minutes before and just after the accident, *1262 and no gravel, stones or debris was found in the area of the temporary walkway where plaintiff fell.
Defendant also pointed to plaintiffs deposition testimony, wherein plaintiff stated that he did not recall seeing stones or pebbles on the temporary walkway before or after the accident.

In opposition to defendant’s motion, plaintiff argued that his fall was not caused by the presence of a foreign substance on the temporary walkway, but by reason of defendant’s failure to erect a sufficient barrier between the edge of the temporary walkway and the ditch below to prevent plaintiff and other patrons using the walkway from falling through the flexible orange mesh fence into the excavated area under construction.

we find questions of fact exist as to whether defendant maintained the premises in a reasonably safe condition and as to whether it created or had actual or constructive notice of the allegedly dangerous condition.

While defendant claims no notice of debris on the temporary walkway, a jury could reasonably conclude that a substantial cause of plaintiffs injuries was defendant’s failure to provide a more sturdy barrier between the temporary walkway and the excavation area

We also note that Supreme Court did not misconstrue plaintiffs deposition testimony, which is simply unclear as to whether plaintiff slipped on loose stones before or after his foot slid off the side of the temporary walkway.

In addition, even if we were to conclude that plaintiffs expert affidavit submitted in opposition to defendant’s motion was insufficient, as claimed by defendant, questions of fact still preclude summary judgment in defendant’s favor.
Accordingly, Supreme Court properly denied defendant’s motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.
Defendant appeals, and we now affirm.

The plaintiff commenced this action to recover damages for personal injuries she allegedly sustained when she slipped and fell inside a pharmacy operated by the defendant Medicine Plaza, Inc. (hereinafter Medicine Plaza), and owned by the defendant Ilene Realty, LLC.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Kings County (Francois A. Rivera, J.), dated April 29, 2021. The order, insofar as appealed from, granted that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against the defendant Medicine Plaza, Inc.

Medicine Plaza established its prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law dismissing the complaint [*2] insofar as asserted against it through the submission of the transcript of the plaintiff's deposition testimony, which demonstrated that she did not know what caused her to slip and fall
In opposition, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.

Contrary to the plaintiff's contention, neither the expert report which she submitted in opposition, nor the surveillance footage of the accident, were sufficient to raise a triable issue of fact as to the cause of her fall
Accordingly, the Supreme Court properly granted that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against Medicine Plaza.
